findings.detail: The TD-035 fix recommendation reads "Revisit at TD-028's trigger, alongside TD-035's sibling TD-036" — TD-035 is the entry being described, so it points at itself. The intended sibling relationship is TD-035 ↔ TD-036 (both are 'second producer / second contributor' deferrals). In the Risk column, `[TD-028]` uses reference-link syntax with no matching definition, so it renders as literal square brackets, unlike the proper `[ADR-0002](../adr/…)` links used elsewhere in this table. This is a living document whose whole value is that a future reader can follow the cross-references at the revisit trigger; a self-loop and a dead-looking link both cost that reader time at exactly the moment the entry is supposed to pay off.
findings.summary: TD-035 names itself as its own sibling, and [TD-028] is not a live link

findings.detail: Factoring `\(?` out of the alternation means `\bfrom` is now also allowed to be followed by an open paren, but there is no ESM edge of the shape `from("./x.js")`. The only thing this widens is the false-positive surface: `Array.from("…​.js")` now matches and would enqueue a bogus URL that 404s and fails the test. In practice this is unreachable — a `.js`-suffixed string literal as the sole argument to `Array.from`/`Object.from` does not occur in a Rollup bundle — which is why this is an observation rather than a request. Recording it because the comment above the regex enumerates exactly three intended forms, and the pattern as written admits a fourth that isn't one of them. I confirmed the other false-positive shapes I could construct are already rejected: `"from":"./x.js"` and `from:"./x.js"` both fail because the character after the quote is `:`, not a specifier. I also grepped for `new Worker(` / `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` module edges in `components/`, `services/`, `utils/`, and `hooks/` and found none, so no real edge class is missed by the crawl.
findings.summary: Optional `(` applies to the `from` branch too, matching a syntax form that does not exist
